result.title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
result.summary: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LLM agent 长程交互中的经验记忆筛选，提出 Anchor：定位关键轨迹步骤并抽取候选记忆，在相同上下文下分别带与不带候选重放源决策，据分布偏移幅度与源动作角色一致性决定是否保留，在 ALFWorld、WebShop 上以冻结策略验证收益与 token 成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一上下文重放、有无候选对比」的局部验证范式可能可供核查 LVR 中轨迹贡献分配与经验/记忆保留的判据，但对象为文本 agent 记忆而非视觉 latent 状态，迁移价值需较多核查。
